- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.05) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment or price; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak if sentiment is bullish.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags 1–2 days behind true trend; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to smooth too much; allow 3–5% volatility buffer in forecast range.
